summary: The blinding output scanner raised false alarms on short sealed values inside names, versions and dates, and passed a UTF-16 (or other non-UTF-8) log that held a sealed value.

database_specific.introduced_basis: the root commit of the repository history (the 0.3.0 import) already has the defect; releases before 0.3.0 are not in this history
database_specific.fixed_basis: fixed in 0.4.0 (CHANGELOG 0.4.0; release commit 9870a35 holds the fix); 0.4.0 has no tag and no release manifest

observables: blinding scan verdict of outputs, logs and caches (core.blinding, skills/hep-computing/scripts/audit_blinded_outputs.py)
check_figure verdict of figures (filled areas, 2D histograms, images, figure text)
impact.bias: a false pass: a log in UTF-16 or another non-UTF-8 encoding that contained a sealed value passed (it was read as UTF-8 with replacement), and filled areas, hist2d/pcolormesh cells, images and figure text in the blinded range were not checked; and false alarms: a sealed value with fewer than 3 significant digits matched any equal token (one unrelated log line gave 8 hits for sealed {0, 3})
impact.trigger: a sealed value in a UTF-16 or Latin-1 log, in a figure drawn with fill_between, stackplot, hist2d, pcolormesh, imshow or text; or a short sealed value (0, 3, 0.5, 100) next to run names, versions or dates

outputs.how_to_recognize: the blinding audit's JSON report (stdout, or --report FILE) and scan verdicts; the scanner writes no artifact, and a measurement-spec does not record that it ran

remedy: rescan the outputs and figures of the blinded analysis with a release that has the fix (audit_blinded_outputs.py); a new hit means a blinded value was exposed and goes to the custodian
